clips.description: While Warren Buffett prefers to hold rather than sell stocks, he will sell when he thinks a company's "long-term competitive advantage" has weakened.

clips.title: Buffett and Munger on friendship

clips.description: Warren Buffett explains why knowing your "circle of competence" and detaching from popular opinion are more important than your IQ in investing.

clips.title: Coke and Gillette are "inevitable" in their industries
clips.headline: Coke and Gillette are "inevitable" in their industries
clips.description: Warren Buffett explains why he has confident about the long-term success of Coca-Cola and Gillette.

clips.title: How to know when you're in your "circle of competence"
clips.headline: How to know when you're in your "circle of competence"
clips.description: Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger explain how they determine what types of business they can understand and the importance of knowing the "boundaries of your competence."

clips.title: Buffett on the importance of caring for the body and mind
clips.headline: Buffett on the importance of caring for the body and mind
clips.description: A teacher asks Warren Buffett how to advise students on preparing for retirement. Buffett says the students should treat their minds and bodies like "the only car you're going to have for the rest of your life."

clips.title: Buffett and Munger on expensing stock options

2002.page_description: (May 4, 2002) Eight months after September 11, 2001, Buffett explains how Berkshire and other insurers have begun to protect themselves financially from catastrophic terrorist attacks that could destroy the industry. videos.title: Why Buffett doesn't ask his friends for favors
videos.headline: Why Buffett doesn't ask his friends for favors
videos.description: Warren Buffett responds to a request from an audience member to enlist the support of his "cousin" Jimmy Buffett in saving the trees in the Florida botanical garden and theme park Cypress Gardens.

videos.description: Warren Buffett starts the session with an in-depth lesson on investing, recalling his first stock purchase when he was 11 years old.  He also predicts the U.S. and China won't have a trade war, responds to Elon Musk on the value of competitive "moats," discusses the goals of his health care initiative with Amazon.com and JPMorgan, and assures shareholders Berkshire will still make big deals without him.

videos.description: Warren Buffett explains why he increased Berkshire's stake in Apple by 45 percent and praises the company's big stock buyback. clips.title: Buffett not worried about a trade war with China

clips.title: Buffett sticks by Wells Fargo
clips.headline: Buffett sticks by Wells Fargo
clips.description: Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger say that although Wells Fargo committed a "cardinal sin," it's still a good investment.

clips.title: Buffett takes a hands-off approach with subsidiaries
clips.headline: Buffett takes a hands-off approach with subsidiaries
clips.description: Warren Buffett doesn't participate much in pricing decisions and has only talked three times in the past ten years to one Berkshire CEO.

clips.title: "We'll probably have the CEO within a couple of months"

clips.description: Warren Buffett discusses his hopes for the Berkshire-Amazon-JPMorgan health care venture announced in January. clips.title: Will Trump's tariffs affect Berkshire?

clips.title: Buffett on Musk: "I don't think he wants to take us on in candy"

videos.title: Morning Session - 2019 Meeting
videos.headline: Morning Session - 2019 Meeting
videos.description: Buffett says that while BNSF and GEICO have fallen behind competitors, he's confident they'll be able to make improvements. He also says Kraft Heinz is still a good business, despite a big reduction in the value of its brands and some accounting issues. videos.title: Afternoon Session - 2019 Meeting
videos.headline: Afternoon Session - 2019 Meeting
videos.description: Buffett has a "feeling" the U.K. vote for Brexit was a mistake, but it doesn't dampen his enthusiasm to do a deal there. He also says Berkshire is strong on the environment but won't spend time and money compiling reports for activists, and predicts Elon Musk's plan for Tesla to sell auto insurance won't be successful. "I worry much more about Progressive" as a competitor for Berkshire's GEICO.

videos.headline: The "simple arithmetic" behind a Berkshire buyback

videos.title: Buffett's politics: "I'm a card-carrying capitalist"
videos.headline: Buffett's politics: "I'm a card-carrying capitalist"
videos.description: Warren Buffett says he doesn't speak for Berkshire when he supports a candidate, but he reserves the right to express his own views as an individual. And even though he has recently backed Democrats for the White House, he's not ready to follow the increasingly vocal left wing of the party.

videos.title: Berkshire's Amazon buy isn't a shift away from "value" investing
videos.headline: Berkshire's Amazon buy isn't a shift away from "value" investing
videos.description: After Warren Buffett reveals that one of Berkshire Hathaway's two portfolio managers has bought "some" Amazon stock, he rejects the suggestion it's a sign the company is changing its long-standing investment philosophy. He and Charlie Munger, however, have some regrets over a lost tech opportunity for which they are "atoning."

videos.headline: "Don't go overboard on delayed gratification"
videos.description: Warren Buffett has cultivated an almost miserly image over the years. While he says he was very frugal when he was younger, he has come to believe that all saving and no spending may not be the best way to enjoy life.

videos.title: 2021 Annual Meeting Highlight Reel
videos.headline: 2021 Annual Meeting Highlight Reel
videos.description: Nicknamed "Woodstock for Capitalists," the Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting is a gathering of the company's shareholders presided over by Chairman and CEO Warren Buffett and Vice Chairman Charlie Munger. The Omaha, Nebraska, event gives shareholders a chance to hear Buffett and Munger discuss investing, their economic outlook and life, as well as ask the legendary pair questions.

videos.title: Part 1 - 2021 Meeting
videos.headline: Part 1 - 2021 Meeting
videos.description: Buffett gives new investors a lesson on picking stocks, admits he made a mistake by trimming Berkshire's Apple position, explains why he opposes a shareholder proposal calling for a corporation-wide report on addressing climate change issues, and talks about how free-spending SPACs are making it harder to find good acquisitions.

videos.title: Part 2 - 2021 Meeting
videos.headline: Part 2 - 2021 Meeting
videos.description: Charlie Munger says "of course, I hate the Bitcoin success," calls the popular trading app Robinhood "deeply wrong" for encouraging what he sees as gambling on financial markets, and casually provides what could be a big clue in the mystery of who will succeed Warren Buffett as CEO. Buffett does a post-mortem on Berkshire's unsuccessful health care joint venture and light heartedly overrules his insurance chief on whether to write a policy for an Elon Musk mission to Mars.

videos.title: Why Buffett doesn't recommend buying Berkshire stock
videos.headline: Why Buffett doesn't recommend buying Berkshire stock
videos.description: Warren Buffett explains why he doesn't recommend that people buy Berkshire Hathaway stock, and reveals what he tells them to do instead.

videos.title: "People on the extremes of both sides are a little nuts"
videos.headline: "People on the extremes of both sides are a little nuts"
videos.description: Warren Buffett says Chevron is not an "evil company" and he has "no compunction in the least" having Berkshire own a sizable stake in the oil giant. But that doesn't mean he's dismissing concerns about climate change.

videos.title: Buffett: It would be "asinine" for Berkshire to compile a single climate change report
videos.headline: Buffett: It would be "asinine" for Berkshire to compile a single climate change report
videos.description: Warren Buffett explains his opposition to a shareholder proposal, backed by institutional investors, calling on Berkshire to compile a climate change report at the corporate level, saying Berkshire Energy and BNSF are the subsidiaries that can have a real impact, and they're already open about the actions they've been taking to reduce their carbon footprint.

videos.title: Munger: We don't have to agree on "every damn little thing we do"
videos.headline: Munger: We don't have to agree on "every damn little thing we do"
videos.description: Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger say they don't agree on everything but have "never gotten mad at each other."

videos.title: Buffett admits selling some Apple shares was "probably a mistake"
videos.headline: Buffett admits selling some Apple shares was "probably a mistake"
videos.description: As he praises Apple CEO Tim Cook as "one of the best managers in the world" and the company's iPhone as a "product that people absolutely love," Warren Buffett says it was probably a mistake to trim Berkshire's enormous stake in the company last year, and that Charlie Munger let him know it at the time.

videos.title: Berkshire can't compete with free-spending SPACs
videos.headline: Berkshire can't compete with free-spending SPACs
videos.description: Warren Buffett says the recent popularity of SPACs has made it even harder to find good companies to buy at an acceptable price. Since they have to return money to investors after two years if they haven't done a deal, SPACs have an incentive to overspend.

videos.title: Buffett's favorite quote on the dangers of gambling on stocks
videos.headline: Buffett's favorite quote on the dangers of gambling on stocks
videos.description: Warren Buffett cites a quote from economist John Maynard Keynes as he talks about how many newcomers are treating the stock market as a casino. Charlie Munger complains it's shameful that some professionals are taking advantage of what he calls "the suckers."

videos.title: Munger: Bernie Sanders has won
videos.headline: Munger: Bernie Sanders has won
videos.description: Charlie Munger explains why he thinks progressive Senator Bernie Sanders "has basically won" his fight to reduce wealth inequality, although "he did it by accident."

videos.title: Munger: "Of course, I hate the Bitcoin success"
videos.headline: Munger: "Of course, I hate the Bitcoin success"
videos.description: While Warren Buffett decides to adopt a former Nebraska governor's standard response to "dodge" a question about enormous gains for cryptocurrencies, Charlie Munger doesn't hold back his long-standing criticism of a currency he thinks is "so useful to kidnappers and extortionists."

videos.title: Would Berkshire insure an Elon Musk mission to Mars?
videos.headline: Would Berkshire insure an Elon Musk mission to Mars?
videos.description: Insurance chief Ajit Jain has no problem saying no to the hypothetical question, but Warren Buffett thinks a deal could be done, for a price.

videos.title: Buffett on cutting back Berkshire's bank holdings
videos.headline: Buffett on cutting back Berkshire's bank holdings
videos.description: Warren Buffett says that he likes banks "generally" and thinks they're in "far, far better shape than 10 or 15 years ago," but "didn't like the proportion we had to the possible risk" last year.

videos.title: America's health care "tapeworm" won
videos.headline: America's health care "tapeworm" won
videos.description: Warren Buffett does a post-mortem on why Berkshire's health care joint venture with JPMorgan Chase and Amazon disbanded without making any dent in how much the U.S. is paying for medical care.

videos.title: "Greg will keep the culture"
videos.headline: "Greg will keep the culture"
videos.description: In a discussion about Berkshire Hathaway's future, Charlie Munger appears to unintentionally reveal who has been designated to eventually replace Warren Buffett as CEO.

videos.title: Robinhood takes advantage of "gambling instincts"
videos.headline: Robinhood takes advantage of "gambling instincts"
videos.description: Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger discuss the popular Robinhood trading app, accusing it of encouraging its customers to make short-term bets on stocks and options. Munger calls it "deeply wrong."

videos.title: 2023 Annual Meeting Highlight Reel
videos.headline: 2023 Annual Meeting Highlight Reel
videos.description: Nicknamed "Woodstock for Capitalists," the Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting is a gathering of the company's shareholders presided over by Chairman and CEO Warren Buffett and Vice Chairman Charlie Munger. The Omaha, Nebraska, event gives shareholders a chance to hear Buffett and Munger discuss investing, their economic outlook and life, as well as ask the legendary pair questions.

videos.title: Morning Session - 2023 Meeting
videos.headline: Morning Session - 2023 Meeting
videos.description: In the morning session, Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger discuss recent bank failures and what Washington needs to do to restore depositors' confidence, the hype surrounding artificial intelligence, and their concerns over growing economic tensions between the United States and China.

videos.title: Afternoon Session - 2023 Meeting
videos.headline: Afternoon Session - 2023 Meeting
videos.description: In the afternoon session, Warren Buffett argues that the executives of failed banks need to be punished and squelches speculation that Berkshire's growing stake in Occidental Petroleum could lead to a bid to buy all of the oil giant. Charlie Munger explains why Elon Musk doesn't need to "overestimate" himself and accepts that his grandchildren probably won't see the world exactly as he does.

videos.title: 'Catastrophic' if FDIC didn't backstop SVB deposits
videos.headline: 'Catastrophic' if FDIC didn't backstop SVB deposits
videos.description: Warren Buffett explains why he thinks its was "inevitable" and necessary for the FDIC to guarantee all deposits at the failed Silicon Valley Bank, even if they were above the formal $250,000 limit.

videos.title: 'Poor messaging' is making Americans worry about their bank deposits
videos.headline: 'Poor messaging' is making Americans worry about their bank deposits
videos.description: Warren Buffett argues Washington should abandon its stated, but not always observed, $250,000 limit on bank deposit insurance and explicitly guarantee that no American will lose any money due to the failure of a U.S. bank.

videos.title: Bad bankers should be punished
videos.headline: Bad bankers should be punished
videos.description: Using the failure of First Republic after making mistakes in "plain sight" as an example, Warren Buffett argues that when a bank gets in trouble, "both the CEO and the directors should suffer." And despite his overall concerns about bank stocks, Buffett says he is sticking with Berkshire's big Bank of America stake because he proposed the $5 billion investment that helped it when it was struggling more than a decade ago.

videos.title: Munger: 'Old-fashioned intelligence works pretty well'
videos.headline: Munger: 'Old-fashioned intelligence works pretty well'
videos.description: Charlie Munger is skeptical of some of the artificial intelligence hype, while Warren Buffett is worried that it can't be "uninvented" if things go wrong.

videos.title: Buffett rules out Occidental Petroleum acquisition
videos.headline: Buffett rules out Occidental Petroleum acquisition
videos.description: In the middle of a discussion about Occidental Petroleum's oil drilling in the Permian Basin, Warren Buffett definitively rules out a Berkshire bid to take control of the oil giant, squelching speculation prompted by its steadily growing OXY stake.

videos.title: Buffett worries about Paramount's future in streaming business
videos.headline: Buffett worries about Paramount's future in streaming business
videos.description: Warren Buffett won't say why Berkshire Hathaway owns a stake in Paramount Global despite his concerns about heavy price competition in the unpredictable video streaming market.

videos.title: Buffett: We don't own too many Apple shares
videos.headline: Buffett: We don't own too many Apple shares
videos.description: Warren Buffett dismisses criticism that Berkshire's portfolio is dominated by its Apple shares, arguing the position should be evaluated in the broader context of both the stocks and companies it owns. In addition, he says, it's a "better business" than any of its fully-owned subsidiaries. On top of that, Charlie Munger thinks experts are wrong to advocate for what he calls the "deworsification" of investments.

videos.title: U.S.-China economic tensions are 'stupid, stupid, stupid'
videos.headline: U.S.-China economic tensions are 'stupid, stupid, stupid'
videos.description: Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger call on the leaders of both the U.S. and China to step back from the growing economic tensions between the two countries and embrace mutually-beneficial trading.

videos.title: 'I do not sign a will until my children have read it'
videos.headline: 'I do not sign a will until my children have read it'
videos.description: Warren Buffett says parents are making a terrible mistake if their grown children are not involved in their estate planning.

videos.title: Raiders won't have enough money to target Berkshire after Buffett
videos.headline: Raiders won't have enough money to target Berkshire after Buffett
videos.description: Warren Buffett says he does think about what will happen when he no longer controls Berkshire, but doesn't "worry enormously" because no one will have enough money to take over the company.

videos.title: Buffett: America needs a 'wartime' strategy for clean energy
videos.headline: Buffett: America needs a 'wartime' strategy for clean energy
videos.description: Warren Buffett argues that the U.S. needs to "reorient the resources" of the country to achieve energy transformation, just as it did to win World War II. But he worries it may not be possible to recreate that kind of effort under our current democratic system.

videos.title: Never make an emotional investing decision
videos.headline: Never make an emotional investing decision
videos.description: Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger explain why you should be a "no emotion" person when it comes to making financial decisions.

videos.title: Elon Musk doesn't need to 'overestimate' himself
videos.headline: Elon Musk doesn't need to 'overestimate' himself
videos.description: Charlie Munger thinks Elon Musk doesn't need to "overestimate" himself because he is a very talented dreamer who "likes taking on the impossible job and doing it." He and Warren Buffett agree they would rather tackle easy jobs.

videos.title: Hard to predict if there will be electric vehicle winners
videos.headline: Hard to predict if there will be electric vehicle winners
videos.description: Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger think the automobile industry's transition to electric vehicles is fascinating, but are reluctant to invest, with Buffett saying, "I think I know where Apple is going to be in five or ten years, but I don't know where the car companies are going to be in five or ten years."

videos.title: 'Not everything that should happen does happen'
videos.headline: 'Not everything that should happen does happen'
videos.description: After UK regulators move to block Microsoft's proposed acquisition of video game maker Activision Blizzard, Warren Buffett won't say whether he has given up on his arbitrage bet that the deal would go through. But he acknowledges it is not looking good, despite Microsoft's "more than halfway" efforts to address antitrust concerns on both sides of the Atlantic.

videos.title: 'We love our business'
videos.headline: 'We love our business'
videos.description: In response to a question about the "hardest part of his business," Warren Buffett says he "works with the greatest group of people he can imagine" in "ideal working conditions."

videos.title: Munger: I accept that my grandchildren won't think the way I do
videos.headline: Munger: I accept that my grandchildren won't think the way I do
videos.description: Charlie Munger says he tries to set a good example for his grandchildren but is "philosophical" about them not thinking exactly the way he does. He also knows he needs to "pretend that I like some of the boyfriends and girlfriends I don't like."

videos.title: Morning Session - 2024 Meeting
videos.headline: Morning Session - 2024 Meeting
videos.description: In the morning session , Warren Buffett, and Berkshire Vice Chairmen Greg Abel and Ajit Jain discuss Berkshire's sale of 13% of its Apple stock holdings, the prospect of higher capital gains taxes, and what Buffett would have done with one more day with Charlie Munger before he died.

videos.title: Afternoon Session - 2024 Meeting
videos.headline: Afternoon Session - 2024 Meeting
videos.description: In the afternoon session , Warren Buffett reveals Berkshire has sold its entire stake in Paramount Global at a loss. He and Vice Chairman Greg Abel also cover the generosity of Berkshire shareholders, the fine points of drafting a will, and Abel's future role as the company's CEO after Buffett is no longer in charge.

videos.title: Buffett: Prospect of higher tax rate in the future made sale of Apple shares more attractive now
videos.headline: Buffett: Prospect of higher tax rate in the future made sale of Apple shares more attractive now
videos.description: Warren Buffett says that while Berkshire sold 13% of its Apple stake in the first quarter, he expects the iPhone maker will remain the company's biggest equity holding. He also expects that the capital gains tax rate will be going higher in the future as the U.S. tackles its deficit, and while Berkshire generally doesn't mind paying taxes, shareholders may appreciate that some Apple shares were sold at the current 21% rate, before tax bite gets deeper.

videos.title: AI could make financial scams a 'growth industry'
videos.headline: AI could make financial scams a 'growth industry'
videos.description: Warren Buffett describes seeing a convincing AI-generated video of himself that has him worried the technology will make financial scams much more convincing.

videos.title: Jain: Fraud is pushing the price of insurance higher in Florida
videos.headline: Jain: Fraud is pushing the price of insurance higher in Florida
videos.description: Ajit Jain, Berkshire Hathaway's insurance chief, says fraud and severe weather are driving insurance prices higher in Florida. He is, however, optimistic Berkshire will still be able to operate profitably there as the state addresses the fraud problem.

videos.title: Reducing collisions with driverless cars would be good for society but may be bad for GEICO
videos.headline: Reducing collisions with driverless cars would be good for society but may be bad for GEICO
videos.description: Warren Buffett says that if Tesla's Elon Musk is able to reach his goal of reducing collisions by 50% with driverless technology it would be good for society and bad for insurers, "but good for society is what we're looking for." Insurance chief Ajit Jain points out that while there may be fewer collisions the cost of each collision is rising, so driverless cars may not generate the savings Musk envisions.

videos.title: Buffett: We sold entire Paramount stake at a loss
videos.headline: Buffett: We sold entire Paramount stake at a loss
videos.description: Warren Buffett reveals that Berkshire Hathaway has sold its entire remaining stake in Paramount Global and "we lost quite a bit of money." He takes 100% responsibility for the position but says the experience has helped him learn more about what people do with their leisure time and how that is affecting entertainment companies.

2024.page_description: (May 4, 2024) In the first shareholders meeting since the death of Charlie Munger, Warren Buffett answers questions with Vice Chairmen Greg Abel and Ajit Jain by his side. Buffett talks about how his expectation the capital gains tax rate will be rising in future years contributed to his decision to sell 13% of Berkshire's Apple stock holdings. They also cover Buffett's willingness to invest in Canada, why he is concerned that AI could lead to more financial scams, and he takes full responsibility for losing "a lot of money" after selling the remainder of the company's stake in Paramount Global.

videos.title: Morning Session - 2025 Meeting
videos.headline: Morning Session - 2025 Meeting
videos.description: In the morning session , Warren Buffett, and Berkshire Vice Chairmen Greg Abel and Ajit Jain discuss tariffs and trade, the company's long-term plans for its Japanese stock holdings, and why investors need to stay calm amid stock market swings that Buffett calls minor when compared much bigger moves over the decades.

videos.title: Afternoon Session - 2025 Meeting

videos.description: As the afternoon session is ending, Warren Buffett surprises everyone with his intention to step down as Berkshire's CEO at the end of the year. videos.headline: Buffett 'celebrates' Greg Abel and Apple's Tim Cook

videos.description: Ajit Jain describes how Berkshire eventually did its 2026 deal with Japan's highly respected insurer Tokio Marine after years of trying.

videos.title: Abel: We're patient but will act decisively when the time is right

videos.slug: Clip 26-06 - Abel: We're patient but will act decisively when the time is right

videos.title: Why it's important to 'just say no'

videos.title: 'Depends on the price'

videos.title: Buffett: I 'understand' fewer businesses these days
videos.headline: Buffett: I 'understand' fewer businesses these days
videos.description: Warren Buffett tells CNBC's Becky Quick it is a difficult time to find suitable investments for Berkshire, in part because there are fewer businesses he "understands" as technology becomes more complicated. videos.title: 'We've never had people in a more gambling mood than now'
videos.headline: 'We've never had people in a more gambling mood than now'

videos.slug: Clip 26-10 - 'We've never had people in a more gambling mood than now'

videos.title: How Abel will handle underperforming managers
videos.headline: How Abel will handle underperforming managers

videos.title: Abel has no plans to break up Berkshire

videos.description: Greg Abel explains why he doesn't expect to ever break Berkshire Hathaway into separate companies or groups.

2026.page_description: (May 2, 2026) In his first shareholders meeting as Berkshire Hathaway's new CEO, Greg Abel stresses that he will maintain the company's long-standing culture, especially its rejection of a centralized bureaucracy. While Warren Buffett sits on the arena floor with his fellow directors, he does speak briefly to praise the board's decision a year before to name Abel as his successor.
